description: A cat owner must decide whether to arrange a long-weekend pet-sitting exchange with a neighbor and finalize the exact care, meal compensation, medication, and key-handoff terms after a kitchen-table check-in with the people involved.

shared_context.S1: Mara needs someone to care for her cat over the long weekend from Friday evening through Monday morning.
shared_context.S2: Mara will make the final call about the arrangement and its terms.
shared_context.S3: Several people at the kitchen-table check-in have discussed helping with the cat.
shared_context.S4: As part of the usual planning check-in, Mara asks each person for relevant availability, costs, care instructions, and access details before agreeing.
shared_context.S5: The check-in follows a routine recorded-statement practice: each person gives their own availability, offer, or advice as a formal statement before the next person speaks, and Mara waits for all four statements before finalizing.
shared_context.S6: Mara records each person's exact terms and any exact care or building requirement in the final verbal agreement.

PF1.text: Eli can care for the cat from Friday at 18:00 until Monday at 08:00 and will do it in exchange for exactly three homemade freezer meals from Mara.

PF2.text: Tessa can provide paid care for the same Friday 18:00 to Monday 08:00 window for exactly $120, an alternative she has not yet mentioned to Mara.

PF3.text: The cat's veterinary clinic told Jon that the cat's medicine must be given at exactly 08:00 and 20:00, with food, during the weekend; Jon has not yet shared this instruction with Mara.

PF4.text: The building manager told Rina that unattended keys and lockboxes are not allowed, so the apartment key must be handed to the sitter in person by Friday at 17:00; Rina has not yet told Mara.

acceptance_conditions: Eli must be selected as the caregiver.
The care window must be Friday 18:00 through Monday 08:00.
Mara must provide exactly three homemade freezer meals as compensation.
The $120 paid-care alternative must be recorded for comparison.
The cat's medicine must be scheduled at exactly 08:00 and 20:00 with food.
The key must be handed to the sitter in person by Friday 17:00.
The settlement must include explicit meal-exchange, medication-care, and in-person-key-handoff commitments.
The final justification must cite PF1, PF2, PF3, and PF4.

content_checks.C4: decisions['medication_schedule'] in ['08:00 and 20:00 with food', '08:00 and 20:00 daily with food', 'Medicine must be given at exactly 08:00 and 20:00, with food, during the weekend', 'Medicine must be given at exactly 08:00 and 20:00 with food throughout the weekend']
content_checks.C5: decisions['key_handoff_by'] in ['Friday 17:00 in person', 'Friday 17:00, in person', 'In person by Friday at 17:00', 'In person by Friday at 5:00 PM', 'Friday at 5:00 PM, in person']
content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] in ['meal_exchange', 'compensation'] and c['target'] == 'Eli' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: decisions['care_window'] in ['Friday 18:00-Monday 08:00', 'Friday 18:00 through Monday 08:00', 'Friday 6 PM through Monday 8 AM', 'Friday 6 PM-Monday 8 AM']
content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] in ['medication_care', 'medication_commitment', 'medication', 'medication_instructions'] and c['target'] == 'Eli' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any(c['type'] in ['in_person_key_handoff', 'key_handoff', 'access'] and c['target'] == 'Eli' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Eli's exact availability selects him, fixes the Friday 18:00-Monday 08:00 window, changes compensation to exactly three freezer meals, and supplies the meal-exchange commitment.
Tessa's exact alternative changes the comparison record from no concrete paid benchmark to exactly $120.
The clinic instruction changes medication from an unspecified routine to exactly 08:00 and 20:00 with food and creates the medication-care commitment.
The building rule changes key access from an unspecified arrangement to an in-person handoff by exactly Friday 17:00 and creates the key-handoff commitment.
